solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some of the military police suppressing resistance

indicators.note: the police hold the resistance down inside them

explanation.surface: Military police keeping a resistance movement down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Military police' reads as one unit, but the definition stops at 'military': a corps is one body of the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by part: a corps is one formation within an army, a portion of the armed forces.

clue.text: Fraud importing right grain

indicators.note: the fraud brings R in, holding it inside

explanation.surface: A trade swindle over a shipment of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Importing' sounds like trade, which suits grain, but here it only means taking something inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: in British use corn covers wheat, barley and oats, the cereal crop in general, not just maize.

clue.text: Nonsense about old supporter

indicators.note: the nonsense goes around O

explanation.surface: Someone talking rubbish about a long-time fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan; to root for a team is to support it, and a root also holds a plant up.
explanation.definitionFit: A root supports a plant, anchoring it in the ground.

clue.text: Lightweight training gear? Pays good money, sparing nothing, to secure one

indicators.note: leaving out, so the O is dropped
the shortened phrase holds I inside it

blocks.note: to shell out = to pay a lot
O = nothing, dropped from SHELLS OUT to leave SHELLSUT

explanation.surface: A shopper paying top price for lightweight sportswear.
explanation.walkthrough: A shell suit is a shiny nylon tracksuit, a British fashion of the late 1980s. The question mark flags that it is worn more for show than for training.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell suit is a light nylon tracksuit, nominally sports gear.

clue.text: Why you may be using the stairs to leave the ground

definitions.text: Why you may be using the stairs
definitions.note: the first definition reads LIFT OFF as a phrase, the lift being switched off

blocks.clueFragment: Why you may be using the stairs
blocks.note: the lift (elevator) is off, so you walk

explanation.surface: Someone climbing stairs as if about to take flight.
explanation.walkthrough: A lift is the British word for an elevator; when it is off, you take the stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a lift that is switched off sends you to the stairs, and a rocket rising from its pad is the verb phrase.

clue.text: Instrumentalists ignoring power levels

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out of account, so the P is left out of PLAYERS

explanation.surface: Musicians paying no attention to the volume levels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power levels' reads as one phrase about amplifiers; the split falls after 'power'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rock strata or cake tiers stacked one on another are both layers and levels.

clue.text: Attractive article removed from Italian car

indicators.note: A is taken out of the car's name

explanation.surface: A handsome piece taken off an Italian car.
explanation.walkthrough: Fit meaning good-looking is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, fit means sexually attractive.

clue.text: Extravert banned departure

blocks.note: out = not allowed, as in 'that's out'

explanation.surface: An exuberant person thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extravert' works as an adjective here, like outgoing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone sociable who seeks company, the opposite of shy.

clue.text: At liberty to ditch an award at soccer

blocks.note: to kick a habit is to ditch it

explanation.surface: A player free to turn down a football trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Award' suggests a trophy, but in football a free kick is awarded by the referee.
explanation.definitionFit: A free kick is awarded to a team after a foul.

clue.text: Former Queen in castle with unknown quantity of birds

definitions.note: a rookery is a colony of birds, so 'of birds' describes it

blocks.note: the rook is the castle in chess
ER = Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A late queen in a castle, surrounded by birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen and castle are both chess pieces, which makes the surface feel like a board game. 'In' here means alongside, not inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookery is a colony of rooks or other birds.

clue.text: Name part of what IT leverages

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the following words

explanation.surface: Naming one element of how IT gets its leverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals on IT make it look like an abbreviation; they do not matter to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name of a book, film or piece.

clue.text: Fear to observe reminder of the time?

blocks.note: to clock is British slang for to notice

explanation.surface: Dread at seeing how late it has got.
explanation.walkthrough: To clock someone is British slang for to notice them. The question mark admits an alarm clock is a pointed reminder, not a gentle one.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful description: the bedside device rings to tell you the hour has come, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Woodworker to complain over log

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second

blocks.note: to log data is to enter it

explanation.surface: A woodworker grumbling about a piece of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Next to a woodworker, 'log' wants to be timber; it is the verb, to record.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the tradesperson who builds and repairs wooden structures, from roof beams to cupboards.

clue.text: Weapon annoyed Bob

blocks.note: to bob is to bow the head

explanation.surface: A weapon that has upset someone called Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital makes Bob look like a man's name; it is the verb, a quick bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the medieval bow mounted crosswise on a stock, firing bolts, is one kind of weapon.

clue.text: Revealing it limits male fashions

indicators.note: IT forms the limits, the two ends, around the rest

explanation.surface: A revealing style that holds back men's fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revealing' is the definition in the sense of a daring outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the clothing sense: a low neckline showing more skin than propriety allows.

clue.text: Gossip is odd of us

explanation.surface: Complaining that the gossip about us is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' tempts toward odd letters; it is RUM, a British word for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: unverified talk passed from person to person.

clue.text: Endless frostiness after element of sarcastic humour

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped
the frost piece comes after the element

explanation.surface: A cold, dry wit in a sarcastic remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element of' reads as 'part of' and invites a hidden word; element is the whole chemical element IRON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironic humour says the opposite of what it means, close to sarcasm.

clue.text: Entertainment venue about to lay off last American

indicators.note: the last letter is dismissed

blocks.note: circa = about; losing its last letter leaves CIRC

explanation.surface: A theatre about to make its last American worker redundant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last American' looks like one phrase; 'last' belongs to the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the big top, or the ring and tiers inside it, where clowns and acrobats perform.

clue.text: Shovel dirt actively? Not for long

indicators.note: the letters are set in motion

explanation.surface: Instructions to dig hard, though not for long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shovel' looks like the instruction; it is fodder, and 'actively' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain paraphrase: a fad or a mayfly's life lasts only a brief time.

clue.text: Produce Republican during arrest

indicators.note: R comes in the middle of the arrest

blocks.note: a cop = an arrest, as in 'it's a fair cop'

explanation.surface: A Republican producing something while being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: Cop as a noun for an arrest is British slang, from 'it's a fair cop'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, reading produce as the noun: what a farm yields in a season, such as wheat or apples.

clue.text: This writer will have a large breakfast?

explanation.surface: The setter announcing a big breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A large breakfast' reads as a full English; the definition is only 'breakfast?', one example of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast is one example of a meal, as the question mark signals.

clue.text: Warning sound? Lead back around shelter

indicators.note: the lead symbol is turned round
the turned symbol goes round the shelter

blocks.note: Pb, the chemical symbol for lead
the lee is the sheltered side

explanation.surface: An alarm going off while someone leads the way back to a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' wants to be the verb, to guide; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleep is an electronic tone, often a warning.

clue.text: Odd bits of prime steak dish, perhaps

indicators.note: take the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Choice scraps of prime steak cooked into a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime steak' reads as a cut of beef, but 'steak' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak pie is one kind of pie, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Small group putting bed ahead of lake

indicators.note: to put something somewhere is to place it, so the bed is set in position before the lake
the bed comes before the lake

explanation.surface: A few friends pitching camp beds beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Erie is the crossword's favourite lake; 'putting' and 'ahead of' together just fix the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with a flavour: a close, rather exclusive circle of people sharing an interest.

clue.text: Observe intelligence and endless sense in action

indicators.note: a word without its end has lost its final letter, so SENSE becomes SENS
the remaining letters are set moving

blocks.note: endless leaves SENS, rearranged to NESS

explanation.surface: Advice to watch intelligence and good sense at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sense in action' reads as practical wisdom; it is two instructions, first cut, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to see an event happen with your own eyes, as at a crime scene.

clue.text: Hold off beginning to pirouette in dance

indicators.note: only the first letter is taken
that letter goes inside the dance

explanation.surface: A dancer delaying the start of a pirouette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold off' reads as delay; here it means fend off.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to drive back an attacker or keep an advance at bay.
